design_detail: Systematic review with random-effects meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42021224850; RevMan 5.4.1) of placebo-controlled randomized trials of any medication for methamphetamine or amphetamine withdrawal in people with a DSM or ICD diagnosis of use disorder or withdrawal. Nine trials (six medications) met the criteria; six trials of four medications (amineptine, mirtazapine, modafinil, amantadine) were pooled. Outcomes: discontinuation, global state, withdrawal symptoms, craving and adverse events; pooled both as 'any pharmacotherapy' and by medication. Risk of bias by RoB 2 and certainty by GRADE.
can_establish: How much randomized evidence existed up to December 2020 on medications for methamphetamine or amphetamine withdrawal, how small and biased it is, and that no medication other than amineptine (two small trials, very low to low certainty) separated from placebo on any pooled outcome.
cannot_establish: That any of the six medications is ineffective (the pooled intervals are wide and most cells rest on one trial), whether any medication is safe in this population (adverse events were counted by arm in one trial only), the absolute size of any effect (arm-level counts are only in unread supplementary forest plots), or effects beyond the short withdrawal period (no follow-up outcomes were synthesized).

sample.recruitment: Not applicable at review level. The included trials were run in the USA (3), Thailand (3), Australia (2) and Iran (1): Australian public outpatient drug and alcohol services and short-stay residential withdrawal units; Thai inpatient drug treatment centres and a specialised probation centre; US inpatient or residential research units (three human laboratory crossover studies); and an Iranian outpatient service with weekly visits (Table 1).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Included: randomized trials in humans of any medication for methamphetamine or amphetamine withdrawal, with or without treatment as usual or psychological treatment, in participants diagnosed with methamphetamine or amphetamine use disorder or withdrawal by DSM or ICD criteria; use of other substances allowed if methamphetamine or amphetamine was the primary drug of concern and the trial did not require concurrent dependence on another substance; a control arm not receiving the intervention, with identical adjunctive treatment in both arms (Methods › 2.2). Three of nine eligible trials were not pooled because they reported none of the review's outcomes in usable form (Results › 3.1).
sample.demographics: Mean trial size 27 participants. About 88% men according to the text (one trial did not report sex); the counts in Table 1 give 198 of 230 (86%; editors' calculation). Mean ages range from 18.5 and 19.6 years in the two Thai amineptine trials to 42.8 years in a US laboratory study. Baseline methamphetamine use, where reported, ranged from 13.1 to 22.4 days per month (Table 1).
sample.attrition: Not applicable at review level. Discontinuation is itself an outcome. Table 1 gives the number reaching each trial's primary endpoint: from 11 of 19 (58%) to 35 of 42 (83%); not reported for the three human laboratory studies.
sample.selection_effects: The evidence base is nine small trials. Both amineptine trials come from the same Thai research group and setting (overlapping author lists, references 51 and 54), enrolled young, almost entirely male inpatients (mean ages 18.5 and 19.6; 97% and 93% men) and gave low-dose lorazepam to both arms. One mirtazapine trial was run in a probation centre with an all-male sample. The amantadine trial enrolled people already more than 3 weeks abstinent, so it concerns a post-acute phase rather than acute withdrawal. Women make up roughly an eighth of participants.

exposure.measurement: The exposure is the assigned study medication, as given in each trial (Table 1). Trial conditions: mirtazapine 15 mg nightly for 2 nights then 30 mg for 12 nights (Cruickshank 2008), or 15 to 60 mg daily titrated over 14 days and not exceeding 30 mg in practice (Kongsakon 2005); modafinil 200 mg daily for 5 days then 100 mg for 2 days (Lee 2013), or a single 200 mg dose in a crossover laboratory study (Mahoney 2012); amineptine 150 mg twice daily for 14 days (Jittiwutikan 1997) or for 5 days (Srisurapanont 1999); ibudilast 10 or 25 mg twice daily for 5 days (Birath 2017); varenicline 0, 1 or 2 mg twice daily for 7 days with crossover (Kalechstein 2014); amantadine 100 mg daily for 28 days (Modarresi 2018).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only, as listed above; treatment periods ranged from a single dose to 28 days. Participants' baseline methamphetamine use is reported for five trials only (13.1 to 22.4 days per month).
exposure.polysubstance: Other substance use was allowed if methamphetamine or amphetamine was the primary drug of concern; no synthesis by co-use. Adjunctive treatment given to both arms included low-dose lorazepam and supportive care in both amineptine trials, narrative-therapy counselling in one mirtazapine trial and symptomatic therapy in the amantadine trial; four trials reported no adjunct or provided none (Table 1).
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Not applicable as an exposure; trials enrolled people at the start of withdrawal (inpatient or residential units) except the amantadine trial, which enrolled people more than 3 weeks abstinent.

comparison.controls: Placebo in all nine trials, with the same adjunctive treatment as the active arm (Results › 3.2; Table 1).
comparison.matching: Not applicable at review level (randomized comparisons). The review's risk-of-bias assessment found problems with the randomization process, including baseline imbalances, in five of nine trials (Results › 3.3).
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: Same populations as the active arms.

outcomes.instruments: Discontinuation: number of participants not remaining enrolled at the primary endpoint. Global state: Clinical Global Impression (two amineptine trials) or Brief Symptom Inventory Global Severity Index (one mirtazapine trial). Withdrawal symptoms: Amphetamine Withdrawal Questionnaire (AWQ), Amphetamine Cessation Symptoms Assessment (ACSA) or Amphetamine Selective Severity Assessment; the AWQ was used when a trial reported several. Craving: the craving scale of the Questionnaire for Evaluating Cocaine Craving and Related Responses (sign reversed to align direction) or a 100 mm visual analogue scale. Safety: adverse events by arm (Methods › 2.6; Results › 3.6 to 3.9).
outcomes.validity_norms: The AWQ is a 10-item scale based on DSM-IV withdrawal criteria; the ACSA is a 16-item scale; the Amphetamine Selective Severity Assessment is the cocaine scale with the drug name changed. The authors note that the Clinical Global Impression dates from the 1970s and call for updated, validated outcome scales (Discussion › 4.4).
outcomes.operationalization: Benefit was defined as fewer discontinuations or lower symptom, craving or global-severity scores than placebo at each trial's endpoint; harm as more adverse events. No outcome after the withdrawal period was synthesized.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None. 17 counts the rows of Table 2 (five outcome domains, by medication and in total); 7 of them pool two or more trials and 10 are single-trial estimates. Significance threshold p = 0.05 throughout.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not applicable at review level. Two reviewers screened titles, abstracts and full texts independently and extracted data independently, with a third reviewer for disagreements (Methods › 2.4, 2.5). The paper does not say whether the RoB 2 and GRADE judgments were made in duplicate (the PROSPERO record planned two independent assessors).

analysis.effect_sizes: Random-effects meta-analysis; relative risks (Mantel–Haenszel) for dichotomous and, per the Methods, standardized mean differences (inverse variance) for continuous outcomes, with 95% CIs (Table 2). Discontinuation: any medication RR 0.70 (0.40 to 1.23), 6 trials, 186 participants, I2 18%, p = 0.21, GRADE very low; amineptine 0.22 (0.07 to 0.72), 2 trials, 74, I2 58%, p = 0.01, very low; mirtazapine 0.96 (0.48 to 1.92), 2 trials, 51, I2 0%, very low; modafinil 0.67 (0.22 to 2.03), 1 trial, 19; amantadine 1.33 (0.34 to 5.24), 1 trial, 42. Global state (labelled mean difference in Table 2): any medication -0.24 (-0.73 to 0.25), 3 trials, 103, I2 69%, very low; amineptine -0.49 (-0.80 to -0.17), 2 trials, 72, I2 0%, low; mirtazapine 0.30 (-0.22 to 0.25), 1 trial, 31. The Results text gives different values for the same comparisons as SMDs: overall -0.34 (-1.06 to 0.25), p = 0.39; amineptine -0.70 (-1.18 to -0.22), p = 0.004; mirtazapine 0.42 (-0.30 to 1.15), p = 0.36. Withdrawal symptoms (SMD): any medication 0.17 (-0.43 to 0.77), 3 trials, 93, I2 49%, p = 0.58, GRADE low; amineptine -0.26 (-0.86 to 0.34); mirtazapine 0.17 (-0.54 to 0.89); modafinil 0.86 (-0.09 to 1.82). Craving (SMD): any medication 0.34 (-0.77 to 1.45), 2 trials, 48, I2 71%, p = 0.55, very low; amineptine -0.19 (-0.92 to 0.54); modafinil 0.95 (-0.01 to 1.92). Adverse events: one trial (amantadine), RR 2.47 (0.76 to 8.03), 35 participants, p = 0.13, very low. Positive values on symptom, craving and global-state scales favour placebo. Absolute risk differences could not be computed: arm-level counts appear only in the supplementary forest plots, which were not read.
analysis.preregistration_detail: PROSPERO CRD42021224850, read in its current version (2.0, 4 July 2025, whose flagged changes concern only review stage, publication status and dates): first submitted 9 December 2020, registered 7 January 2021, review start date given as 21 December 2020; the paper calls the registration prospective. Unacknowledged differences between the record and the paper: dichotomous outcomes were to be analysed as odds ratios but relative risks were used; the record's context section limits language to English while the paper says no language limits were applied; planned comparisons by time period (up to 4 weeks, 4 to 12 weeks, over 12 weeks) and planned subgroup analyses (setting, treatment-seeking status, dose, control type) are not reported; the record lists PubMed, the Cochrane Library, PROSPERO and TRIP among sources, while the paper lists MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, EMBASE and ClinicalTrials.gov; the record excluded comorbid substance use or mental health conditions, which the paper does not mention. All five outcomes are primary in the record.
analysis.selective_reporting: The sensitivity analysis replacing the AWQ with other withdrawal scales is described as non-significant with data not shown. Forest plots, the full GRADE summary-of-findings table and the search strategy are only in supplements (not read). One mirtazapine trial that reported a benefit on withdrawal symptoms (AWQ, p = 0.03) could not be pooled because only medians were available, and the pooled withdrawal estimate therefore omits a positive trial. Safety data were absent in four trials and narrative in four.
analysis.power: Not addressed formally. Trials averaged 27 participants; every medication-specific estimate rests on one or two trials, and the authors call for better-powered trials. Intervals such as RR 0.40 to 1.23 for discontinuation and SMD -0.43 to 0.77 for withdrawal symptoms include both moderate benefit and harm.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Nine small placebo-controlled trials (242 participants) of six medications; six trials of four medications could be pooled. Only amineptine, in two small trials from one Thai group in young male inpatients, separated from placebo: fewer discontinuations (RR 0.22, 0.07 to 0.72, I2 58%, very low certainty) and better global state (Table 2 MD -0.49, -0.80 to -0.17; text SMD -0.70, -1.18 to -0.22; low certainty). Mirtazapine, modafinil and amantadine did not differ from placebo on any pooled outcome, with wide intervals; modafinil's single-trial estimates for withdrawal symptoms (SMD 0.86, -0.09 to 1.82) and craving (0.95, -0.01 to 1.92) lean towards placebo. Six of nine trials were at high risk of bias. Comparative safety could not be assessed.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The conclusion that the evidence is insufficient to show any medication is effective, and also insufficient to rule any out (Abstract; Discussion, 1st paragraph; Conclusion), matches the data and is appropriately cautious. Gaps: (1) the abstract reports the amineptine global-state effect as MD -0.49, which matches Table 2 but not the SMD of -0.70 in the Results text or the Methods' statement that continuous outcomes were pooled as SMDs, and a raw mean difference cannot validly pool the two different scales used; (2) the Discussion (4.1) moves from the amineptine result to suggesting that drugs with a methamphetamine-like but longer-acting profile may be the more promising research path, which rests on two trials from one group with high or unclear risk of bias and very low to low certainty; (3) the abstract's 'first comprehensive meta-analysis since 2008' frame does not mention that the pooled 'any pharmacotherapy' estimates combine four drugs with different mechanisms and an outpatient post-acute trial with acute inpatient ones.

timeline.event: Shoptaw et al., Cochrane review of treatment for amphetamine withdrawal: four randomized trials, no medication supported (cited by this review as the last comprehensive meta-analysis; the introduction names the agents as amineptine and modafinil, but by this review's own Table 1 the four early trials tested amineptine and mirtazapine).
Pennay and Lee, narrative review of the evidence base for treating methamphetamine withdrawal (cited as reaching a similar conclusion).
Siefried et al., systematic review of medications for methamphetamine or amphetamine dependence from the same research group (cited as reference 61; it addresses dependence rather than withdrawal).
This review: nine trials of six medications, six pooled; no medication supported except amineptine, which is no longer marketed.

replication.where_it_stands: The most recent systematic review of medications for methamphetamine withdrawal read for the encyclopedia; its search ended in December 2020. Four of its nine trials (all pre-2009) were in the earlier Cochrane review, so the two reviews are not independent evidence. Pooled estimates rest on one or two trials per drug, and the only positive drug (amineptine) has been withdrawn from the market. Claims about withdrawal pharmacotherapy should cite this review for the state of the evidence and not for any drug-specific effect size.

funding.funder: No funding section in the article. The conflict-of-interest statement says the first author is funded by an NDARC PhD scholarship and by NCCRED; open-access publication was covered by the Wiley–UNSW agreement (Acknowledgment). The PROSPERO record lists NCCRED (funded by the Australian Commonwealth Department of Health) and NDARC (supported by the Australian Government Department of Health) as funding sources.
funding.declared_conflicts: One author, as Director of NDARC, has received unrestricted research funding from Indivior and Seqirus (printed as 'Sequiiris'); no other conflicts declared.
funding.affiliations_note: Authors from NDARC (UNSW Sydney), St Vincent's Hospital Sydney Alcohol and Drug Service, NCCRED, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital and the NSW Drug and Alcohol Clinical Research and Improvement Network. One review author (McKetin) is a co-author of an included trial (Lee et al., 2013, modafinil), and the senior author (Siefried) led the group's 2020 review on dependence; no procedure for review authors assessing their own trials is described. Recorded as flags for closer reading.

what_would_settle_it: An adequately powered, multi-site, double-blind placebo-controlled trial of a candidate withdrawal medication in people entering methamphetamine withdrawal, with a registered primary outcome on a validated withdrawal scale, prespecified retention and adverse-event reporting by arm, inclusion of women, and follow-up into post-withdrawal treatment engagement and use.

domains.domain: 1. PICO components in research question and inclusion criteria
domains.note: Population, intervention, placebo or same-adjunct comparator and five outcomes specified.

domains.domain: 2. Protocol registered before the review, deviations justified (critical)
domains.note: PROSPERO record submitted 9 December 2020 and registered 7 January 2021, around the review's stated start date of 21 December 2020; deviations (relative risks instead of planned odds ratios, planned time-period and subgroup analyses not done, different databases and language rule) are not acknowledged.
Restriction to randomized trials as the highest level of evidence is stated and its consequence discussed (Discussion › 4.4).

Four databases, ClinicalTrials.gov and reference lists, no language limits, example strategy in a supplement; no grey literature or expert contact; database date ranges printed inconsistently; search ended December 2020, 19 months before online publication.
Two reviewers independently, third reviewer for disagreements.
Two reviewers independently with a piloted template.

domains.domain: 7. List of excluded studies with justification (critical)
domains.note: The 11 full texts excluded are cited (references 38 to 48), but reasons are not given study by study in the text; the PRISMA figure is an image.

domains.domain: 8. Included studies described in adequate detail
domains.note: Table 1 gives setting, n, sex, age, baseline use, drug, dose, duration, comparator and adjuncts; diagnostic criteria, outcome timing and each trial's outcomes are not tabulated.

domains.domain: 9. Satisfactory risk-of-bias assessment of included studies (critical)
domains.note: RoB 2 applied to every trial and domains summarized (Figure 2 is an image); whether judgments were made in duplicate is not stated.

domains.domain: 10. Funding sources of included studies reported
domains.note: Funding was extracted (Methods › 2.5) but is not reported.

Random-effects pooling in RevMan is appropriate in itself, but the effect measure for global state is inconsistent (mean difference in the abstract and Table 2, SMD in the Methods and Results, with different values), a raw mean difference across two different scales would be invalid, Table 2 prints a point estimate outside its own interval, causes of heterogeneity (I2 up to 71%) were not investigated, and the 'any pharmacotherapy' totals combine four drugs with different mechanisms and different phases of withdrawal.

domains.domain: 12. Impact of risk of bias on pooled results assessed
domains.note: No sensitivity analysis by risk of bias, although six of nine trials were at high risk; risk of bias enters only through GRADE downgrading.

domains.domain: 13. Risk of bias accounted for in interpretation (critical)
domains.note: Conclusions are framed by low to very low certainty and high risk of bias throughout.
I2 is reported but heterogeneity is not explored; planned subgroup analyses were not done.
Not assessed or discussed; the GRADE domains listed in the Methods omit publication bias.

domains.domain: 16. Conflicts of interest and funding reported
domains.note: Conflicts and the first author's funding are declared; the review's funding appears in the PROSPERO record, not in the article.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Two critical items are 'no' (inconsistent and partly invalid effect measures for global state with unexplored heterogeneity; no consideration of publication bias), which places the review at critically low confidence under AMSTAR 2. This judgment concerns the specific pooled numbers, above all the global-state estimates, which appear in two incompatible versions. The review's qualitative conclusion, that nine small trials do not establish any effective withdrawal medication, is robust to these problems: the search was broad and duplicated, risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and the certainty ratings are low to very low.

key_findings.finding: Nine placebo-controlled randomized trials of six medications met the criteria (242 participants as reported): mirtazapine 2, modafinil 2, amineptine 2, ibudilast 1, varenicline 1, amantadine 1; conducted in the USA (3), Thailand (3), Australia (2) and Iran (1); mean size 27 participants; about 88% men by the text (86% by Table 1 counts, editors' calculation).
key_findings.locator: Abstract › Key Findings; Results › 3.1 Included studies; Table 1

key_findings.finding: Six trials of four medications (186 participants: 89 on medication, 97 on placebo) were pooled; three (ibudilast, varenicline, one modafinil laboratory study) reported none of the review's outcomes in usable form.

Risk of bias (RoB 2): 1 trial low, 2 some concerns, 6 high. Selective reporting affected 6 of 9 trials, the randomization process 5, deviations from intended interventions 3, missing outcome data 2, outcome measurement 1.
key_findings.note: The trial-by-trial judgments are only in Figure 2, an image whose values were not extracted.

key_findings.finding: Discontinuation, any medication versus placebo: RR 0.70 (95% CI 0.40 to 1.23), 6 trials, 186 participants, I2 18%, p = 0.21; GRADE very low.
key_findings.note: The text gives 188 people; Table 2 and the participant counts give 186.

key_findings.finding: Discontinuation by medication: amineptine RR 0.22 (0.07 to 0.72), 2 trials, 74 participants, I2 58%, p = 0.01, GRADE very low (downgraded for serious risk of bias and very serious imprecision); mirtazapine 0.96 (0.48 to 1.92), 2 trials, 51, I2 0%, very low; modafinil 0.67 (0.22 to 2.03), 1 trial, 19; amantadine 1.33 (0.34 to 5.24), 1 trial, 42.
key_findings.locator: Table 2; Results › 3.5; 3.10 GRADE quality of evidence

key_findings.finding: Global state (Clinical Global Impression or BSI Global Severity Index), Table 2: any medication -0.24 (-0.73 to 0.25), 3 trials, 103 participants, I2 69%, GRADE very low; amineptine -0.49 (-0.80 to -0.17), 2 trials, 72, I2 0%, GRADE low; mirtazapine 0.30 (-0.22 to 0.25), 1 trial, 31. Table 2 labels these as mean differences.
key_findings.note: Results › 3.6 reports the same comparisons as SMDs with different values: overall -0.34 (-1.06 to 0.25), p = 0.39; amineptine -0.70 (-1.18 to -0.22), p = 0.004; mirtazapine 0.42 (-0.30 to 1.15), p = 0.36. The mirtazapine value in Table 2 lies outside its own interval. Which set is correct cannot be decided from the article.

key_findings.finding: Withdrawal symptoms (AWQ, ACSA): any medication SMD 0.17 (-0.43 to 0.77), 3 trials, 93 participants, I2 49%, p = 0.58, GRADE low; amineptine -0.26 (-0.86 to 0.34), 43; mirtazapine 0.17 (-0.54 to 0.89), 31; modafinil 0.86 (-0.09 to 1.82), 19 (positive values favour placebo). Replacing the AWQ with the other scales left results non-significant (data not shown).
A second mirtazapine trial (Kongsakon 2005, 20 participants) reported lower AWQ withdrawal scores than placebo (p = 0.03) but could not be pooled because only medians were reported.
Craving: any medication SMD 0.34 (-0.77 to 1.45), 2 trials, 48 participants, I2 71% (p = 0.06), p = 0.55, GRADE very low; amineptine -0.19 (-0.92 to 0.54), 29; modafinil 0.95 (-0.01 to 1.92), 19.

Safety: only the amantadine trial reported adverse events by arm (RR 2.47, 0.76 to 8.03, 35 participants, p = 0.13, very low certainty). Three trials described adverse events in text only (modafinil: none, with lethargy and disturbed sleep in both arms; mirtazapine: no serious events, mild headache, nausea, vomiting; varenicline: no neuropsychiatric or dose-related events, without data); four reported nothing on safety.

Unpooled results: amantadine reduced fatigue versus placebo (p < 0.001, no effect size); modafinil shortened sleep latency versus baseline but not versus placebo after crossover; two mirtazapine trials found no sleep benefit, one reporting more night awakenings than placebo; varenicline gave faster visual reaction time (p = 0.025, eta-squared 0.103) without benefit on working memory or sustained attention; ibudilast improved 2 of 12 Continuous Performance Test-II measures.
key_findings.locator: Results › 3.11 Findings from studies not included in the meta-analysis

key_findings.finding: Amineptine, the only medication separating from placebo, was voluntarily withdrawn from the market by its manufacturer in 1999 after reports of hepatotoxicity and non-medical use, and was never approved in several jurisdictions including the USA, according to the review.

Searches covered MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL and EMBASE to December 2020, plus ClinicalTrials.gov and the reference lists of included papers, without language limits; the search is reported as having yielded 20 results, 11 of which did not meet the inclusion criteria.
key_findings.note: The review does not say at which stage the 20 were assessed: the text gives only the yield and the 11 exclusions, and the screening counts are in the PRISMA flow diagram, which is an image whose values were not extracted. Two of the 11 excluded citations are conference abstracts with e-page numbers, so not all 11 can have been full-text reports.

reporting_issues.issue: Global-state estimates differ between Table 2 (and the abstract) and the Results text: amineptine -0.49 (-0.80 to -0.17) labelled a mean difference versus SMD -0.70 (-1.18 to -0.22); overall -0.24 (-0.73 to 0.25) versus SMD -0.34 (-1.06 to 0.25); mirtazapine 0.30 (-0.22 to 0.25) versus SMD 0.42 (-0.30 to 1.15). The Methods state continuous outcomes were pooled as SMDs; the abstract's Approach says weighted mean differences.
reporting_issues.consequence: The amineptine global-state effect, which the abstract reports, exists in two incompatible versions; a raw mean difference pooling the Clinical Global Impression with the BSI Global Severity Index would not be valid. Claims should cite the direction only, or both values with this caveat.

reporting_issues.issue: In Table 2 the mirtazapine global-state point estimate (0.30) lies outside its own interval (-0.22 to 0.25). Editors' check: the Results text's overall SMD of -0.34 is not centred in its interval (-1.06 to 0.25; midpoint about -0.41), whereas every other estimate in Table 2 is centred in its interval on the appropriate scale.
reporting_issues.consequence: At least two printed global-state figures contain typographical errors; their correct values cannot be reconstructed without the supplementary forest plots.

reporting_issues.issue: Participant totals do not reconcile: 242 participants in the abstract and Results; Table 1 sums to 241; the arm allocations (129 on medication plus 138 on placebo) sum to 267, and the 48% and 52% are computed on 267, because crossover participants are counted in both arms. The discontinuation section says 188 people while Table 2 gives 186.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; the pooled analyses use 186. Any claim quoting the size of the evidence base should say 'about 240 participants in nine trials'.

reporting_issues.issue: Several Table 1 percentages do not match their counts (Cruickshank: 16 of 31 shown as 53% and 20 of 31 as 63%; Lee: 12 of 19 shown as 65%; Kalechstein: 18 of 26 shown as 71%), and the text's 'approximately 88%' men does not match the 86% the Table 1 counts give (editors' calculation).
reporting_issues.consequence: Small transcription errors; they weaken confidence in the extraction but do not change any conclusion.

reporting_issues.issue: Table 1 gives identical baseline methamphetamine use, 18.3 (SD 8.9) days per month, for two different trials (Lee 2013 and Mahoney 2012).
reporting_issues.consequence: Probably a copying error for one of the two trials; baseline use figures in Table 1 should be checked against the primary papers before being cited.

reporting_issues.issue: The search periods differ between the abstract (MEDLINE 1966, CINAHL 1982, PsycINFO 1806, EMBASE 1947, all to 2020) and the Methods (MEDLINE 1964, PsycINFO 1967, CINAHL 1961, EMBASE 1974, to December 2020).
reporting_issues.consequence: The exact coverage of the search cannot be stated; it is unlikely to matter, since the earliest included trial is from 1997.

reporting_issues.issue: The introduction says the 2008 Cochrane review identified four trials of amineptine and modafinil, but by this review's own Table 1 the only trials published by 2008 tested amineptine (1997, 1999) and mirtazapine (2005, 2008); the modafinil trials date from 2012 and 2013, and the discussion's count of five later trials fits the amineptine-mirtazapine reading.
reporting_issues.consequence: The description of the earlier review's content is internally contradicted; the same group's 2020 review (Siefried et al.) lists the Cochrane review's trials as the 1997 amineptine trial and the 2005 and 2008 mirtazapine trials plus one other. Claims about what the Cochrane review covered should be taken from that review, not from this summary.

reporting_issues.issue: The withdrawal-symptom result is printed as 'SEM 0.17' (Results › 3.7), evidently for SMD; the craving and withdrawal sections are otherwise consistent with Table 2.
The Methods list the GRADE domains as risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness and imprecision, omitting publication bias, and publication bias is not assessed anywhere in the review.
reporting_issues.consequence: The low and very low certainty ratings are, if anything, generous on this domain; with one or two small trials per drug, small-study effects cannot be excluded.

reporting_issues.issue: The Results state that three trials were not pooled because they did not report the review's 'primary outcomes', but the Methods do not designate any outcome as primary (the PROSPERO record lists all five as primary). The citation given for the screening software (reference 29) is a 1995 criminology book.
reporting_issues.consequence: Reporting looseness; no effect on the estimates.

reporting_issues.issue: Differences from the registered protocol (odds ratios planned, relative risks used; time-period and subgroup analyses planned, not reported; English-language limit in the record versus no limit in the paper; different database list) are not acknowledged in the article.
reporting_issues.consequence: Readers cannot tell from the article which analyses were planned; the deviations do not appear to favour any medication. Status of this item: the article side is confirmed by both readers (Methods 2.1 calls the registration prospective, 2.8 and Table 2 report relative risks, 2.3 states that no language restriction was applied and lists MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, EMBASE and ClinicalTrials.gov, no time-period or subgroup analyses are reported, and no deviation from the protocol is acknowledged). The registry side is single-reader: the PROSPERO record was not accessible in the second reading, so the planned odds ratios, the planned time-period and subgroup analyses, the English-language limit, the database list and the comorbidity exclusion have not been re-checked.

reporting_issues.issue: The 1999 voluntary market withdrawal of amineptine is stated in Discussion 4.1 and cited to references 64 and 65, which the reference list gives as a 1996 report of two cases of amineptine-induced liver injury and a 1998 report of amineptine and midazolam dependence. Both predate 1999, so neither can document the withdrawal, and the date itself carries no source in the review.
reporting_issues.consequence: The year must not be cited through this review. Any claim that dates the withdrawal needs a primary regulatory or manufacturer source, or should say that the review states it. The same group's 2020 review (siefried_2020, Results › Antidepressants, 1st paragraph) says only that amineptine was never approved by the US regulator and has been suspended in other jurisdictions, with no date and no reference, so it does not corroborate the year.

reporting_issues.issue: The safety counts do not reconcile between sections. Results 3.9 accounts for eight of the nine trials (one reporting adverse events by arm, three describing them in text, four reporting nothing; the 1997 amineptine trial is not mentioned), while Discussion 4.2 says four trials reported no safety data and another four gave only a narrative description.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor: it does not affect the statement that only one trial reported adverse events by arm, which both sections agree on, but the narrative-only count should be taken as three or four with the discrepancy noted.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC10083934 (all sections, Tables 1 and 2 rendered as text, conflict-of-interest statement, acknowledgment, article notes and reference list read; Figure 1 (PRISMA flow) and Figure 2 (risk-of-bias graph) are images and their values were not extracted; supplementary Figures S1 and S2 and Tables S1 and S2 not read).
